steps.text: Dossoles – Casino

steps.name: Skeptical Customer
steps.text: Hey, what’re y’all looking at over there?

steps.name: Excited Customer
steps.text: You gotta come check this out! The boss is throwing his hat into the ring with one of the gamblers. Hurry, the winner's about to be decided!

steps.name: Skeptical Customer
steps.text: What's the big deal? Who's the foolish fella sittin' across the table anyway? Never heard of the legendary boss at the gaming table?

steps.name: Excited Customer
steps.text: Hahaha, come over here. You'll see.

steps.name: Excited Customer
steps.text: That's the guy.

steps.name: Skeptical Customer
steps.text: What?! That guy? He's got the balls to come back here?

spans.text: guy? He's got the balls to come back here?

steps.name: Excited Customer
steps.text: Pssh, the fact that he's got the balls to sit at the table means the Mayor already decided to write off everything he's done.

steps.name: Dealer
steps.text: River. Any bets?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Thanks, I'll check.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: You sure?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Haha, what is there to be unsure about?

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: That's the guy you're going in with, boy?

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: What difference does it make if you can keep one of his hands attached to his wrist? Look at him now. Wandering the streets, eyes completely dead. But, the moment he walks into a casino, tch... His eyes light back up.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: C'mon, this is Dossoles, and people like that are everywhere.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Then why don't I see you sitting down at any of the other tables?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Well... The poor guy's only got one hand left. Life's gonna be pretty hard if he loses that one too.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Who knows how he lost his other hand. For all you know, a guy with his character probably lost it at some gambling table.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Actually... he lost it in a war.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: He used to be a soldier under my father's command. I've known him since I was little.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Molly, bring me another glass.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Give it up. You can't beat my hand.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Sorry about this, boss.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: (Flips cards over)

steps.name: Excited Customer
steps.text: Woah... That's a hell of a hand.

steps.name: Skeptical Customer
steps.text: Royal... Flush? Haha, my god, that kid's got some absurd luck.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: (Molly, think this kid's...?)

steps.name: Dealer
steps.text: (I didn't see him making any suspicious moves. Do I need to call someone?)

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: (No, forget it.)

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: (I hear Señora Sanchez has some plans for him... So we'll consider this a favor.)

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: You're sure that guy's hand is worth so much to you? You'd have to give up all your chips. A pretty high price, if I do say so myself.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Hahaha! Boss, if someone offered you this much money for a hand, you'd be the last man at this table to hesitate.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Molly, untie him and let them leave.

steps.name: Dealer
steps.text: Sure.

steps.name: Casino Boss
steps.text: Make sure you check every one of the guy's fingers. With that price tag, we can't afford to be careless.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Haha, how could I question your integrity? Your good name is known far and wide.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: As for you, Señor... You look like you haven't had a good night's rest in a long, long time. Go home, enjoy a nice shower, and sleep.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Ernesto, I...

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Sorry, boss. I still have some urgent business to attend to, so I've gotta go.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Ernesto! Ernesto! Wait!

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Hmm?

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: I kept calling for you, but you didn't answer so I had to follow you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Señor, did you need anything else from me?

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: I don't know if you still remember me or not, but we met before. You were still young, barely up to my knees. Your mother was there at the time, leaning against the doorframe just like that.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I do... Of course I remember, Señor José.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: My mother and I barely had a centimo to our names. If you didn't cross an entire warzone to send supplies back home to us, we would've had a hard time making it through that winter.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: I was only following Señor Pancho's orders. I never deserved to stay in your memory so long, Ernesto.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: After I joined the army, I wanted to find you and thank you, but my father told me that you had been wounded and subsequently discharged.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: That's right. There's no place on the battlefield for a man short a hand.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Did you come back to meet... Or rather, visit Señor Pancho?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Yes. I'll see him at noon.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: I'll leave you to it then. Don't be late on my account.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Ah... There are so many things in the past I thought I'd never remember again. But when I saw you, those days turned crystal-clear once more.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I thought I had forgotten it all myself...

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Señor José... You should give up gambling.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Haha, you have the wrong idea. I'm going home, back to where I belong. After all you went through to bail me out, how could I dare to go back?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: If, and only if you really need it, you can come looking for me. I can't guarantee you a whole lot of work, but it should be enough to get you back on your feet.

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Alright...

steps.name: Down-and-out Gambler
steps.text: Thank you, Ernesto.
Dossoles – Prison

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: You're late. I waited a whole hour for you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Sorry, Dad. Something came up along the way and slowed me down.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Are you trying to make excuses for your tardiness, Ernesto?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: The fault is mine. I'm very sorry, Father.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Hmph. Looks like a year at Rhodes Island has plucked some of those flowery words from your mouth.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: There aren't so many people at Rhodes Island who need to be flattered, so I don't have to speak the way I did before.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Really now? You never mentioned any of that in your letters.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Because it's not important, I didn't feel a need to bring it up.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I suppose there's not much you could say on that silly little sheet of paper.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Right. Actually, there are a lot of things I want to tell you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: But, Rhodes Island's business is more complicated than I thought, and it's hard for me to find the time to sit down and write a comprehensive letter. The best I can do is to pick out some important things and go over them briefly.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Dad, did you know that Rhodes Island has several operators from Bolívar? One of them goes by Señora Dobermann. She was a soldier like you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: And I opened up a weapons shop. There are lots of knowledgeable hands there, and I always enjoy doing business with them.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Also, there's the Doctor and Señora Kal'tsit––

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Enough, Ernesto! What did I tell you before you left?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Don't worry, Dad. I've been taking good care of Rafaela. She's in excellent health and enjoying her life.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I've heard that same story from you half a million times on your little scraps of paper.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: She... is a grown woman, Dad. There are some things I can't just go asking her.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I said, enough! That's not the only thing I told you!

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Oh... You're talking about that.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I see... right, that.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: I told you to figure out your future, sooner rather than later.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Don't become complacent. Don't squander your talents in pursuit of a cushy life. Have grand ambitions.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I'm definitely going to end up in Bolívar. But it's not time for that yet.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: How long do you intend to wait then? Until your hair turns grey? Until Bolívar is smashed to pieces?!

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Dad, I... I still have doubts to work through. There are still many things I have to make sense of, both about myself, and about Bolívar.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: This is all because I underestimated the influence that Candela woman had on you. I never imagined that even if you left this place and lost contact with her, you'd still cling to her bag of tricks the entire time.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I know you didn't agree with Ms. Candela's way of doing things, Dad, but I have to recognize that she also had her reasons.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: You really take after your mother with all that indecisiveness. Had I known earlier, I would've ignored her pleas and raised you myself. At least that way, you could've at least been a resolute, unflinching soldier.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Mom never did anything wrong. Raising me under those conditions wasn't easy. The hardships and sacrifices she had to go through are more than you could imagine, it's not your place to criticize her.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Sorry, Ernesto.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Dad, do you know who I met on the way here?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Who?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Señor José. He was one of your runners for three years.

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: That one, huh.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Do you remember how many times you had him bring back supplies for me and mom?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: He told me, he still remembers my mother. Not the cold, unmoving version of her in photos, but the version of her that's vivid in his memories.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I thought I was the only one who still remembered her like that...

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Do you think I've never yearned for her in my heart, Ernesto?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Before Mom died, she told me that when she first met you, she had a flower pinned to her chest, and it was the flower that drew you to her from the crowd.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Dad, do you still remember what flower it was?

steps.name: Pancho
steps.text: Don't remember.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: *sigh*...

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: That's too bad. I was hoping you would be able to tell me.

steps.name: Mayor's Bodyguard
steps.text: Please wait, Mr. Ernesto.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Hah, long time no see, Mr. Booker.

steps.name: Mayor's Bodyguard
steps.text: Lady Candela heard that you returned to Dossoles, and hopes to meet with you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: If you don't mind me asking, what does Miss Candela need me for?

steps.name: Mayor's Bodyguard
steps.text: Please get in the car. Lady Candela will let you know once you arrive.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Well... I was planning on paying her a visit anyway. I appreciate the lift, Mr. Booker.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: This is... a wedding venue? This is where Ms. Candela is?

steps.name: Mayor's Bodyguard
steps.text: With me, please. She's waiting at the frontmost table.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: (Taps at the glass with a fork)

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Conductor, would you mind pausing this wonderful melody? I'd like to offer a few words to the new couple.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: During this short half a lifetime of mine, marriage has always been such a distant word. I have loved deeply, but love has never given me the courage to enter such a special contract.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What kind of courage must one find before signing over his hand to another with which he has no blood relation, along with his property, body and soul, and future?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Before the wedding, I asked our groom, Mr. Will, if he was aware of the risks that came with this undertaking, akin to walking into the wilderness naked.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: But, he told me that he would weather any storm just to see that flower on the other side.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: (Raises glass) Go forth then, Mr. Will, and bravely trek into that raging storm. Fill every day and night of her life with happiness.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: May your love be true for all of eternity!

steps.name: Everyone
steps.text: May your love be true!

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: (Squeezes his lips tightly)

steps.name: Mayor's Bodyguard
steps.text: Lady Candela, he's here.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: It's been a while, Ernesto.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Ms. Candela, long time no see. Have you been well?

steps.name: Guest A
steps.text: What is he doing here? The gall of that man, showing up at a wedding reception hosted by Lady Candela...

steps.name: Guest B
steps.text: Shh... Keep your voice down. She invited him here. Remember how she said before the ceremony that she'd bring a special guest?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Ladies and gentlemen, I'm sure you're all familiar with this young man. His name is Ernesto Salas, one of my most capable staff. He used to work in the International Trade Management Department.

steps.name: Guest B
steps.text: Welcome back to Dossoles, Ernesto.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I appreciate the warm reception, sir.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Have you been enjoying your extended vacation, Ernesto?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: There's nothing worth concerning yourself over, Ms. Candela. Though I did run into some unexpected surprises, I've been well overall.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Unexpected surprises? I'd like to hear more.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Your eyes look a little red. Is everything alright?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I've been away too long, and I've forgotten how hard the wind blows along the beach here.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Is that so? I think the wind is pretty tranquil tonight, just the way I like it.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Did you... refloat this boat?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Yes. I planned to decorate it at the end of the year and put it back into use.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Even after all those explosions, even sinking to the bottom, it can still serve?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: It has served me faithfully in the past, so I didn't want to move on. Even now, I still look forward to how it will serve me in the future, and fully believe in its potential.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: You never struck me as the nostalgic type.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: What matters to me isn't how long something has been around, but rather how long it'll last.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Besides, truly worthwhile things aren't afraid to stick around for a while, just like the bottle of rum sitting on the table – produced in my private winery, aged for seven years, the finest batch of that year.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Seven years in the darkness has only served to enhance its aroma.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Would you like to try a glass?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Haha. Thank you, Ms. Candela. Half a glass will do. After being away for so long, I can't hold my liquor as well as before.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: That is fine. Mr. Booker, please pour out half a glass for our guest.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Ah, I can do it myself.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: (Raises eyebrow) Are you no longer accustomed to our way of doing things?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I appreciate it, Mr. Booker.

steps.name: Mayor's Bodyguard
steps.text: Here you go.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Thank you. Now then, Ms. Candela, if you don't mind.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: (Takes a sip from the glass)

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: How is it?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: *cough* *cough* Rich and full-flavored indeed. I would expect nothing less from your discerning tastes.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: But do you like it?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Haha, this came from your personal collection. How have another opinion?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You went to see your father. How's he doing?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Well, he's still in decent health. Thank you for looking after him. I will always remember this favor.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Hmph. I'm sure that stubborn old fossil had some choice words for me, even locked away in prison.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: No, no. If anything, the brunt of his criticism was directed at me, over how I'm nothing like him and don't share his ambitions.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: A pity he's so old and addled he can't even recognize his own son.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Hahaha... Always the joker, Ms. Candela. There's no father out there who couldn't understand his own son.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: You are anything but lacking in ambition. If anything, your sights are higher than just this one city.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: I'm not sure what you mean by that.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Dossoles will not always belong to me. I am getting older, while its glory continues to shine ever brighter. More and more people flock to it, and I am searching for someone.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Someone who can help me defend this light in a world surrounded by feral beasts, someone who can take it much further even after I am gone.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: So, would you like another glass?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: (Strokes the glass in his hand)

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Take this bottle of wine home with you and savor it slowly. Maybe eventually, you will come to appreciate its taste.

steps.name: Bridesmaid A
steps.text: Throw it to me, throw it to me!

steps.name: Groomsman B
steps.text: Yeah, yeah. Hand it over here.

steps.name: Bridesmaid B
steps.text: Huh? Where'd it go?

steps.name: Groomsman A
steps.text: My man, you lobbed that thing.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: What's this?!

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Hahahaha! Looks like I'll be waiting for good news from you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: This... is embarrassing. I'll hand this back to the bride and have her throw it again.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Keep it, and treat it as a good omen. Dossoles has no shortage of fine ladies.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Seems like it's getting dark. If it's not convenient for you to head back right now, you can spend the night at the nearby hotel. I've already asked them to keep a spare room for you.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Thank you for your consideration, Ms. Candela.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: I have other business. See you around.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Hmm? Didn't you have something else you wanted to discuss?

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Ernesto, your life could be a lot more comfortable if you completely cut ties with Bolívar. Have you ever considered that?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: (Shakes head)

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Why not?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Because, its thorns are what brings me joy.

steps.name: Candela
steps.text: Go forth then, Mr. Ernesto, and bravely trek into that raging storm. Fill every day and night of its life with happiness.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Ugh, my head hurts... I haven't had anything this strong in a long time...

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Jeez... Why'd I take the bouquet with me when I left? Well, whatever... I'll just toss it in a trash bin later.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Why are there so many people standing around up there? Señor, excuse me, but would you mind letting me through?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Isn't that the casino from yesterday?

steps.name: Casino Guest
steps.text: Buddy, you'll want to give it a minute. Someone just died in the casino.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Someone died?

steps.name: Casino Guest
steps.text: Some hapless fellow just scored a jackpot. Couldn't handle the stimulation apparently and died on the spot.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Hmm, that's... quite the cruel twist of fate.
A stretcher exits from beneath the magnificent gates of the casino. Ernesto can vaguely make out a human figure beneath the white sheet, his brow furrowing into a frown as he prepares to leave.
Suddenly, a gust of wind lifts up the corner of the cloth, revealing a mutilated arm beneath.

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: (Clenches fist)

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Excuse me, would you mind waiting just a moment?

steps.name: Casino Worker
steps.text: Later, kid. Can't you see that we're busy moving the body?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Just a moment of your time, please.

steps.name: Casino Worker
steps.text: What are you... Haha, a flower? You're pinning a flower to his chest? What, did you know this guy?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Yes.

steps.name: Casino Worker
steps.text: Who was he then?

steps.name: Tequila
steps.text: Nobody special. Just an ordinary Bolívarian.
